Definition: to be soft or pliable, i.e. (figuratively) effeminate or luxurious
BiblicalUsage: The word means soft, delicate, luxurious — and it is used both ways. Moses warns of the tender and delicate woman who would not set foot on the ground for delicateness, whose eye turns evil toward her own family in the siege; and Isaiah promises that if you delight yourself in the LORD, He will cause you to ride on the high places of the earth. The same softness is a curse in the one place and a delight in the other.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for softness carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the difference between delighting in luxury and delighting in the LORD.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
